payload.summary: Two amendments describe issues that are already fixed in the current code, while the save-migration amendment identifies a real backward-compatibility regression caused by introducing reserve-gated shrimp lifecycle transitions without seeding legacy saves.

votes.rationale: `shrimp_feeding()` already converts onto the organic-matter routing basis before touching detritus: it computes `food_demand_route_g`, `periph_consumed_route_g`, then `detritus_demand_route_g`, and compares/subtracts that against `fine_detritus_g_total`. The claimed periphyton-biomass-vs-detritus mismatch is not present in the current implementation.

The cited test already works on the routing/organic-matter basis. It converts periphyton removal with `algae_detrital_mass_g(...)`, compares `periphyton_consumed_route_g + detritus_consumed_route_g` to `max_daily_intake_route_g`, and checks `daily_food_consumed_g` against the same routed sum. It is not summing incompatible mass bases anymore.

The v3→v4 migration is a no-op, so missing `animal.reserve_g` deserializes to `0.0`, but reserve is now the mandatory funding source for hatching and juvenile maturation. That means a valid legacy save with near-hatch eggs or mature-ready juveniles will load and then immediately diverge from prior behavior because those transitions fail until reserve is rebuilt. The existing save/load test hard-codes that zero-reserve outcome, so this compatibility bug would remain undetected.
